title: Second damage: mortal falls block remitted peace and Spirit-gifts; lighter faults do not
source_text: XLIX. Deinde quum renati vitio suo in atrocia peccata labuntur, tunc benevolentia Dei erga ipsos ita ligata & impedita est, per obicem quem eorum peccata illi ponunt, ut non possit, hoc statu durante, in eos referre remissionem peccatorum, aut pacem & gaudium conscientiae, & similia Spiritus Sancti dona. Nihil tale vero sequitur ex levioribus & quotidianis fidelium peccatis, quae non obstant quominus Deus semper promptus & paratus maneat ad conferendum in eos solita atque ordinaria gratiae suae salutaris effecta & testimonia; nimirum fiduciam remissionis peccatorum, pacem con-scientiae, & laetitiam spiritualem: quamvis peccata etiam levissima, ex se & sua natura, nos reddant incapaces & indignos gratiae divinae donis.
pass_a_gloss: Next, when the regenerate by their own fault fall into atrocious sins, then God’s benevolence toward them is so bound and hindered by the obstacle which their sins place before him, that he cannot, while this state lasts, confer upon them the remission of sins, or peace and joy of conscience, and like gifts of the Holy Spirit. But nothing of the sort follows from the lighter and daily sins of the faithful, which do not hinder God from remaining always ready and prepared to confer upon them the wonted and ordinary effects and testimonies of his saving grace—namely confidence of the remission of sins, peace of conscience, and spiritual gladness: although even the lightest sins, of themselves and by their own nature, render us incapable and unworthy of the gifts of divine grace.
pass_b_english: Atrocious falls bind God’s goodwill: while they last, remission-sense, conscience-peace, and Spirit-gifts are blocked.
Daily lighter faults leave ordinary saving testimonies flowing—though even they deserve unworthiness by nature.

choices.why: Temporary blockade during the mortal fall.
